messages:
maria: quick question — the console p50/p95/p99 for /v1/generate looks fine at the endpoint level, but when I split by route (route_name) the p99s sometimes drop below the endpoint p95. seems impossible.
aj: can you paste a screenshot? is it per-model-variant too or just route split?
maria: screenshot attached (not in thread). it's specifically route split; endpoint totals: p95=420ms p99=980ms. route A p99=350ms, route B p99=360ms, counts add up to endpoint but p99s are lower.
noah: likely a rollup/sampling artifact. our rollup uses tdigest with sample weights, and when we split by tag we drop some sample metadata for a subset of requests (legacy router path). that can invert quantiles.
phil: if the sample weight was set to 0 for some streaming requests we do see lower tails on the split. but dropping requests would normally increase p99, not reduce it. curious.
anya: another theory — the route tag is applied in the ingestion pipeline after we truncate long tails (we have a 2s cap for histogram buckets). if cap applied before tagging, the per-route view sees capped latencies while endpoint uses uncapped raw values.
maria: that would explain it. where in pipeline is the cap enforced? I thought capping happens in the exporter.
noah: capping is done in the collector stage for latency smoothing. collector has two paths: fast-path (no tags) and tagged-path. fast-path still includes very long latencies from cold starts, tagged-path goes through an extra filter that clips >1500ms to 1500ms to reduce noise.
aj: so the endpoint rollup pulls from fast-path, and route rollups pull from tagged-path. mismatch confirmed.
phil: TL;DR: two different sample sources. We should make it explicit in the console and the API. Right now we show a single p99 value with a little route dropdown that silently switches to different sample streams.
anya: proposal: add a small badge next to each split that shows "sample origin: collector-fast | collector-tagged" and add hover text explaining differences. also record the sample_count and sum_of_weights per cell.
maria: yes please +1. Users think numbers are comparable by default.
metrics-bot: note: export pipeline change detected at 2550000000 by eng-infra — collector:tagged-path clip=1500ms
aj: for a short-term fix we can add a tooltip row showing the effective sample_origin for every rollup. long-term: unify paths or add reconciliation logic (prefer rolling up raw values and then annotating).
phil: reconcile idea: compute endpoint quantiles from the union of all sample streams using consistent pre-processing (no cap). it's more expensive but correct.
noah: also worth adding an API flag for callers: `rollup_source=raw|tagged|union`. could be `?rollup_source=union` on the /metrics endpoints.
maria: can someone open a platform ticket for the console UX change (badge + sample_count)? I'd like the product PM to review copy.
anya: I'll open and tag @product. short description: "Dashboard: make sample origin explicit for split rollups; surface sample_count and effective weights per cell"
aj: quick implementation note: backend will emit new dimension `sample_origin` with values `fast` or `tagged` and `sum_weights` and `count` fields on the rollup proto. front-end change should be straightforward.
phil: one more gotcha — rollouts and canaries: when routing policies send 5% traffic to a canary variant without route tag, the canary requests end up in fast-path and inflate endpoint tails. include that in the docs.
maria: ok timeline? UX badge + tooltip = hotfix this week? new backend proto + API flag = next sprint?
noah: I can PR the proto change today. front-end can toggle tooltip using the `sample_origin` if present; otherwise show legacy note.
anya: created ticket PLATFORM-1429 and added notes + screenshot. assigning to @maria for acceptance criteria.
maria: thanks. also we should add a small QA test: create a synthetic route where tagged-path clips at 1500ms and verify splits show different sample_origin and that tooltip explains the discrepancy.
phil: sounds good. :thumbsup:
